lessons.title: Reading an Extract from Pepys's Diary (Simplified)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to understand a simplified extract from Samuel Pepys's diary.
success_criteria: I can say what Pepys saw.
I can say how he felt.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap who Samuel Pepys was from last week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a simplified, age-appropriate extract of Pepys's diary describing the fire, discussing meaning.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about what Pepys saw and felt, using the extract.
key_questions: How do you think he felt?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use evidence from the text in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of a primary source extract — evidence for ENG.R2/HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family what Pepys saw during the fire.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction Recap with a Diary Theme
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve mixed addition/subtraction problems.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model mixed addition/subtraction problems in a diary-page counting context (e.g. pages written).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve a mix of addition and subtraction problems within 20.
key_questions: Is this an adding or taking away problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record mixed operation problem-solving — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.plenary: Recap how to spot addition vs subtraction problems.
lessons.home_link: Make up a mixed problem for your family to solve.

lessons.title: What Makes a Good Eyewitness Account?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why eyewitness accounts are useful to historians.
success_criteria: I can say what an eyewitness is.
I can say why their account is useful.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why Pepys's first-hand account is valuable evidence for historians studying the fire.
lessons.independent_task: Children record why eyewitness accounts like Pepys's diary are useful.
key_questions: Why is Pepys's diary useful to us today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain limitations of eyewitness accounts too (one person's view)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note developing historical enquiry skill regarding sources — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member to recount something they witnessed.

lessons.title: Writing My Own Eyewitness Account
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write their own simple eyewitness account of an imagined event.
success_criteria: I can write what I saw.
I can write how I felt.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Pepys's diary style from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a first-person eyewitness account of an imagined event (e.g. a school event).
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own short eyewitness account of an imagined or real event.
key_questions: How did it make you feel?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note first-person writing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share eyewitness accounts with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write an eyewitness account of something that happened today.

lessons.title: Measuring in Centimetres
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure objects using a ruler in centimetres.
success_criteria: I can use a ruler to measure an object.
I can record the length in centimetres.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap non-standard unit measuring from earlier.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using a ruler correctly to measure length in centimetres.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure classroom objects using rulers, recording lengths in cm.
key_questions: How long is this object in centimetres?
Which is the ruler's zero point?

differentiation.greater_depth: Measure and compare multiple objects, ordering by length

lessons.assessment_notes: Record standard unit measuring skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap measuring accurately with a ruler.
lessons.home_link: Measure objects at home using a ruler.

lessons.title: Comparing Pepys's Account to a Picture Source
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare information from a written source and a picture source.
success_criteria: I can find information in the diary extract.
I can find information in the picture.
I can say if they agree.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing information from the diary extract to a picture of the fire, checking for agreement.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare a diary extract detail to a picture source detail, noting similarities.
key_questions: Does the picture show the same thing?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early source comparison/corroboration skill — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap how sources can be compared.
lessons.home_link: Compare a photo and a description of the same event at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Diary-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read diary/writing themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read diary words.
I can read a sentence about writing.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending diary/writing themed words.
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading diary words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Capacity
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and describe the capacity of containers.
success_criteria: I can say which container holds more/less.
I can use a non-standard unit to measure capacity.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which of two containers might hold more water.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing capacity using water and non-standard units (cups).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the capacity of different containers using cups as a non-standard unit.
key_questions: How many cups filled this container?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record capacity comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the capacity of two containers at home (with permission).

lessons.title: Museum of London: Digital Sources
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a digital resource to find information about the Great Fire.
success_criteria: I can find a fact using a digital resource.
I can record what I found.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we can learn about history using computers/websites.
lessons.main_teaching_input: (If available) explore a simple, curated digital resource about the Great Fire together as a class.
lessons.independent_task: Children record one new fact found using the digital resource.
resources_needed: Digital resource/website (teacher-curated) or printed screenshots if unavailable
key_questions: What new fact did you find?
How is a website different from a book?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early digital research skill and source awareness — evidence for HIST.2/COMP links.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about the Great Fire online together with an adult.

lessons.title: Presenting Pepys's Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a short account of Samuel Pepys's story to the class.
success_criteria: I can say who Pepys was.
I can say one thing he did during the fire.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Pepys.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear short presentation.
lessons.independent_task: Children present a short account of Pepys's story to a small group.
key_questions: What did he do that was useful to us?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and historical knowledge application — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about Samuel Pepys.

lessons.title: Ordering Numbers to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order a set of numbers to 20.
success_criteria: I can order numbers from smallest to largest.
I can order numbers from largest to smallest.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model ordering a scattered set of numbers to 20.
lessons.independent_task: Children order sets of number cards to 20 in both directions.
key_questions: Can you order these from largest to smallest?

differentiation.greater_depth: Order numbers to 30+ including some in words

lessons.assessment_notes: Record ordering skill — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise ordering numbers together at home.

lessons.title: Half-Term 2 Timeline: Placing the Great Fire
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to place the Great Fire of London on a simple historical timeline.
success_criteria: I can find 1666 on a timeline.
I can say if it's a long time ago.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the toy timeline from earlier in the term.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce a simple timeline spanning several centuries, placing 1666 and today on it.
lessons.independent_task: Children add the Great Fire to a class timeline, comparing its distance from today to other events studied.
key_questions: What else is on our timeline?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the concept of centuries in simple terms

lessons.assessment_notes: Note chronological understanding across topics — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the class timeline so far.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how long ago 1666 was compared to your family's history.

lessons.title: Eyewitness Accounts Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about eyewitness accounts learned this week.
success_criteria: I can answer a question about Pepys's diary.
I can say why eyewitness accounts are useful.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quiz-style recap of the week's learning about Pepys and eyewitness accounts.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet/quiz on the week's learning.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and historical recall — evidence for ENG.R2/HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about eyewitness accounts with your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Measuring Length and Capacity, Ordering Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply measuring and ordering skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can measure using a ruler.
I can compare capacity.
I can order numbers to 20.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of measuring length, capacity, and ordering numbers.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 10 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising measuring over the weekend.

lessons.title: Pepys and Eyewitness Accounts: Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about Samuel Pepys and eyewitness accounts learned this week.
success_criteria: I can say who Pepys was.
I can say why his diary is a useful historical source.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Samuel Pepys and Eyewitness Accounts' display combining diary writing and source comparison work from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about Pepys and sources?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, building historical enquiry skills before moving to geography next week — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Samuel Pepys with your family.
